sentences.text: Shri Vibhor Kumar Sahu- learned Counsel for appellant.
Shri Naval Kishor Gupta- learned Counsel for respondent Bhopal Unit, Gwalior.
Heard on the question of admission.
Record of the trial Court has been received in connected Criminal Appeal No.161 of 2024.
Appeal being arguable, is admitted for final hearing.
Heard on IA No.294 of 2024, first application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. moved on behalf of appellant Kamlesh Sharma, seeking suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

Appellant stood convicted under Section 420 of IPC and sentenced to undergo three years' rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs.5,000/-, sentenced to undergo four years' rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs.5,000/- under Section 409 of IPC and sentenced to undergo four years' rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs.10,000/- under Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act,
1988 with default stipulations, vide judgment of conviction and sentence dated 23.12.2023 passed by Special Judge (PC Act) Datia in SC EOW No.01 of 2021.
Learned Counsel for the appellant submits that appellant was Branch Manager for short period of four months from November, 2004 to February, 2005.
It is alleged that appellant has misappropriated Rs.38,000/- which was the difference between cash book and stock.
Further, there was misappropriation with regard to amount of Bardana (jute-bag) in 3125 as the same could not be tallied.
Leaned Counsel submits that conviction is based on audit report given by Surendra Kumar Chaturvedi (PW5).

Learned Counsel contends that the audit report was not produced and proved before the Court rather one special audit note (Ex.P41) was produced by Surendra Kumar Chaturvedi (PW5) which was an extract prepared on the basis of alleged audit report.
No cash book or stock register was seized and produced before the Trial Court.

Learned Counsel referring to Para 7 of Ex.P41, Para 5 of statement of DK Tripathi (PW6), Para 20 and 21 of statement of Deepak Kamlesh Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35693692/
1 Shrivastava (PW-18) and other relevant documents, contends that the audit note specifically mentions to the effect that Govindsharan Shrivastava had not handed over the charge of stock to his successor i.e. appellant Kamlesh Sharma.

sentences.text: Therefore, variance at the cash book and stock could not be attributed to appellant- Kamlesh Sharma.

Learned Counsel further submits that the Investigation Officer himself has not verified the facts stated in extract audit report i.e. audit note (Ex.P41) from cash book and stock of concerned Cooperative Society.
Learned Trial Court ignored aforementioned important aspects of the matter.

Therefore, conviction of appellant for misappropriation,
misconduct, cheating and breach of trust was erroneous.
Learned Counsel for the appellant further contends that impugned judgment passed by learned Trial Court is based on assumption, conjectures and surmises.
The learned Trial Court has committed an error in convicting and sentencing the present appellant without appreciating the prosecution evidence properly.
There are material contradictions and omissions in the evidence of witnesses.
Learned Counsel, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, also submits that the appellant is aged around 67 years.
He is old, sick and infirm person.
He is suffering from various ailments.
He was remained in judicial custody from 31-03-2022 till 22-06-2022 and from date of passing of impugned judgment i.e. 23-12-2023, he is custody.
Fine amount has already been deposited by appellant.
There is no likelihood of early hearing of appeal in n e a r future.
On these grounds, learned Counsel prays that execution of remaining jail sentence of appellant may be suspended and he may be enlarged on bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for respondent- EOW opposes the application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence and prays for its rejection.

Upon hearing learned Counsel for the parties, regard being had to the old-age as well as ailments of the appellant, but without commenting upon rival contentions touching merits of the case, this Court is of the view that application deserves to be allowed.

The Trial Court shall be authorized to grant exemption from attendance to the appellant on any date, on sufficient cause being shown [Chapter XIII Rule 42 Sub-Rule 2 of the M.P. High Court Rules, 2008].
Where the appellant does not appear on the date of his appearance before the Trial Court and no sufficient cause for non-appearance is shown, the Trial Court shall be authorized to issue non-bailable/bailable warrants to secure his attendance under intimation to the Registry of High Court.
The Trial Court shall also proceed under Section 446 of CrPC against such appellant and his surety without any reference to this Court and without any impediment of the order granting bail.

[Chapter XIII Rule 42 Sub-Rule 3 of M.P. High Court Rules, 2008].
On arrest/surrender in compliance with the warrant, the appellant shall be forwarded in custody to undergo remaining sentence of imprisonment under intimation to the Registry of this Court.
Accordingly, IA No.294 of 2024 stands allowed and disposed of.
List for final hearing in due course.
